title: How to view your payslip and read its components
body:
This article describes the generic payslip process followed by most large Indian employers. It is not an Infosys-specific policy; your HR portal and offer letter are the final reference.

Where to find it: monthly payslips are usually published on the employee self-service (HR) portal after payroll is processed, typically around the last working day of the month. You can download a PDF for any past month. On this help desk, signed-in employees can ask the assistant for a specific month (for example "payslip for September 2026") and it will read your demo payslip record.

Common earnings: basic salary, house rent allowance (HRA), and other or special allowances. Variable pay or bonus appears only in the month it is paid.

Common deductions:
- Employee provident fund (EPF): 12% of basic wages, matched by the employer as required under EPF rules.
- Professional tax: a state levy; in Karnataka it is deducted monthly from salaried employees above the state threshold.
- Income tax (TDS): deducted every month based on your declared investments and chosen tax regime.

Gross pay is the total of earnings; net pay is gross minus deductions and is what reaches your bank account.

If something looks wrong (missing allowance, wrong bank account, unexpected TDS jump), raise a payroll ticket with the month and the line item in question. Keep your tax declarations and proofs updated before the payroll cut-off, because late declarations generally change TDS only in later months.

title: Submitting expense and reimbursement claims
body:
This describes a generic corporate reimbursement process, not a published Infosys policy. Eligibility, limits and approval rules are set by your employer's internal policy, which you should check on the HR or finance portal.

Typical steps:
1. Keep the original bill or a clear digital copy. GST invoices should show the vendor's GSTIN, date, amount and tax.
2. Submit the claim on the expense portal under the right category (travel, local conveyance, internet, client entertainment, relocation and so on) and attach the bills.
3. Your manager approves it, then finance verifies the bills against policy.
4. Approved claims are paid with salary or in a separate reimbursement run, depending on the employer.

Tax points worth knowing: some reimbursements, such as certain business travel and official expenses, are not treated as taxable salary when supported by bills, while fixed allowances paid without bills are generally taxable. Your payroll team will show this treatment in your payslip and Form 16.

Common reasons for rejection: missing or unreadable bills, claims filed after the internal deadline, wrong category, duplicate submissions, or amounts above the policy limit.

If a claim is stuck, raise a ticket with the claim ID, submission date and current status. The help desk can see your payslip and leave records but cannot approve claims.

title: Checking your leave balance and applying for leave
body:
This article explains a generic leave process used by many Indian corporates. Leave types, yearly quotas and carry-forward limits are internal policies; check your HR portal for the rules that apply to you.

Check your balance: signed-in employees can ask this help desk "what is my leave balance?" and the assistant will read your demo leave record, which shows earned/privilege leave, sick leave, casual leave and compensatory off, along with the date the balance was last updated.

Applying:
1. Apply on the HR portal before the leave (or as soon as possible for sick leave).
2. Choose the leave type, dates and a short reason. Half days are usually allowed.
3. Your manager approves or rejects it; you get a notification either way.
4. Leave without enough balance usually becomes loss of pay, which reduces salary for those days.

Good to know:
- Public holidays and weekends that fall inside a leave period are usually not counted, but this depends on policy.
- Compensatory off is normally credited only after the manager approves the extra working day, and often has an expiry.
- Earned leave can often be carried forward up to a cap and may be encashed on exit as per policy and law.

If your balance looks wrong after an approval, wait one working day for the sync and then raise a leave ticket with the dates involved.

title: Form 16: when you get it and what it contains
body:
Form 16 is the certificate your employer gives you for income tax deducted from your salary. The rules below come from the Income Tax Department; the way your employer delivers it (portal download or email) is a generic corporate process.

Deadline: under Rule 31 of the Income-tax Rules, the employer must issue Form 16 by 15 June of the financial year that follows the year in which tax was deducted. For example, for salary paid from April 2025 to March 2026, Form 16 is due by 15 June 2026.

Two parts:
- Part A shows your employer's TAN and PAN, your PAN, and the tax deducted and deposited each quarter. It is generated from the government TRACES system.
- Part B shows the salary break-up, exemptions, deductions you claimed and the tax computation.

Changed employers during the year? Each employer issues Part A for the period you worked there. Part B can be issued by each employer or only by the last one.

New name: as of October 2026, the Income-tax Act, 2025 replaces Form 16 with Form No. 130 for tax years under the new law. The 15 June due date continues. Check which form applies to your year before filing.

Use Form 16 together with your Form 26AS / Annual Information Statement when filing your return. If the TDS in Form 16 does not match 26AS, raise a payroll ticket with the quarter and amount.

title: PF: activating your UAN and completing KYC
body:
Your Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued by the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) and stays with you across jobs. Your employer shares it with you at joining; everything else is done on the EPFO member portal or the UMANG app.

Activate your UAN:
1. Open the EPFO member portal (unifiedportal-mem.epfindia.gov.in) and choose "Activate UAN", or use the UMANG app.
2. Enter your UAN, member ID, Aadhaar or PAN, plus your name, date of birth and mobile number.
3. Enter the PIN sent to your mobile to activate. The portal then sends your password by SMS.

Complete KYC:
- Aadhaar: you can self-verify your UAN against Aadhaar with e-KYC on the portal or UMANG, without your employer.
- Bank account: enter the account number and IFSC; an OTP goes to your Aadhaar-linked mobile. After that your employer must approve the bank details, so the status can show "pending" until they do.
- PAN: also seeded through the portal and approved by the employer.

Why it matters: EPFO requires Aadhaar seeded against an activated UAN to file online claims, and complete KYC lets transfers happen automatically when you change jobs.

If your KYC has been pending employer approval for more than a week, raise a ticket in the "PF, tax & gratuity" topic with your UAN and the KYC item that is pending.

title: Transferring your PF balance when you change jobs
body:
This article uses EPFO's published guidance. Your employer only approves requests; the transfer itself is handled by EPFO.

Automatic transfer: if your UAN is activated and your KYC (Aadhaar, bank, PAN) is complete, EPFO generates the transfer automatically when the first contribution from your new employer is received under the same UAN. In that case you usually do not need to file anything.

When you need to file: if you hold an older UAN or member ID that is not linked, or your KYC is incomplete, you file a transfer claim (Form 13). Online, it is available on the member portal under online services; EPFO's FAQ also allows the balance and service from a previous UAN to be moved to the current one through online Form 13. A physical Form 13 can be downloaded from the EPFO website; it must be attested by the authorised signatory of your present or previous employer and submitted to the EPFO field office. Newer EPFO material may refer to the form by an updated name, so check the portal before filing.

Tips:
- Make sure your name, date of birth and gender match across Aadhaar and EPFO records; mismatches are the most common reason for rejection.
- Do not withdraw and re-deposit; transferring keeps your service continuous, which matters for pension and tax on withdrawal.
- Track the claim status on the member portal.

If your new employer has not started PF contributions in your existing UAN, raise a payroll ticket with your UAN.

title: Gratuity: who is eligible and how it is calculated
body:
Gratuity is a statutory lump sum paid when you leave an employer. These rules come from the Ministry of Labour; your employer's exit process (who to contact, how long settlement takes) is internal.

Which law applies: as of October 2026, gratuity is governed by the Code on Social Security, 2020 for payments on or after 21 November 2025. The Ministry's FAQ says service before that date is still governed by the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972.

Eligibility:
- Permanent employees: at least five years of continuous service when employment ends by resignation, retirement or termination.
- The five-year condition does not apply on death or disablement.
- Fixed-term employees: eligible after one year of service under the Code.

Formula: 15 days' wages for every completed year of service, or part of a year above six months, based on the last drawn wages. For monthly-paid staff, one day's wage is the monthly wage divided by 26. In practice: last drawn wages x 15 x years of service / 26.

Ceiling: the maximum gratuity is the amount notified by the Central Government, which is Rs 20 lakh as of October 2026 (raised from Rs 10 lakh after the 2018 amendment).

Worked example: last drawn basic plus DA of Rs 52,000 and 7 years 8 months of service counts as 8 years: 52,000 x 15 x 8 / 26 = Rs 2,40,000.

For questions about your full and final settlement, raise a ticket under "PF, tax & gratuity".

title: Supplier invoices: what Infosys needs on every invoice
body:
Infosys publishes a supplier payments guide that explains its invoice rules. The points below paraphrase the India guide; regional versions (APAC, EMEA, US) differ in some details, so always follow the version and PO terms that apply to you.

Every invoice should include:
- A valid purchase order (PO) number. One invoice should reference only one PO.
- The billed-to name exactly matching the Infosys legal entity that issued the PO.
- Your complete bank details and the invoice currency.
- For India: GSTIN, HSN or SAC codes, a description of goods or services, and GST shown by component (CGST, SGST/UTGST or IGST) with rates and amounts.
- Your PAN (required for domestic vendors).

TDS: Infosys deducts tax at source unless you provide an exemption certificate. If you have a lower-deduction certificate under section 197 of the Income Tax Act, submit it and mention the category on your invoices.

Where to send: send invoices to the Accounts Payable (AP) desk named on your PO, after delivery. An invoice counts as submitted only when AP receives it, and your payment-term clock starts on that date. Do not send invoices to the payment-query or vendor-master mailboxes. The EMEA guide additionally asks for signed and sealed originals and does not accept handwritten or dot-matrix invoices.

Late invoices: the guide states that Infosys is not obliged to pay invoices received more than 180 days after delivery.

Registered vendors can check the status of a specific invoice here by giving the invoice number.

title: Supplier payment terms, payment runs and status queries
body:
This summarises Infosys's published supplier payments guide. Payment terms in your PO or contract always take priority.

Payment terms: terms are set per supplier. Once your invoice is matched against the PO (and receipt of goods or services where applicable), the system calculates the due date from the date AP received the invoice. For example, on Net 30 terms the due date is 30 days after AP receipt. Where terms are not clearly defined, the guide says payment is released at Net 60 from the date the invoice reaches the AP desk.

Payment runs: the guide states that payments are processed in a weekly batch on Thursdays. An invoice that becomes due after the weekly cut-off moves to the following Thursday's run.

Why a payment may be delayed:
- PO number missing, wrong, or more than one PO on the invoice.
- Invoice addressed to a different Infosys entity than the PO.
- GST, PAN or bank details missing or not matching the vendor master.
- Goods or services receipt not yet confirmed by the requesting team.

Payment status: registered vendors with login access can see payment information on the Infosys vendor portal. Payment-status questions go to the P2P helpdesk at Askus_p2p@infosys.com and must be sent from your company email ID, not a personal address. Do not attach new invoices to these queries.

On this help desk, a signed-in vendor can ask "status of invoice <number>" to see the demo invoice record, including any expected payment date.

title: Becoming an Infosys supplier and updating vendor details
body:
Infosys does not publish an open self-registration form for new suppliers. Suppliers are brought on through Infosys procurement, usually when a business team has a need. The points below come from Infosys's supplier payments guide and its Responsible Supply Chain and Supplier Diversity Policy.

Onboarding checks: before empanelment, Infosys runs a third-party assessment that, depending on the vendor type, can cover compliance, adverse media, information security, physical security and sustainability. Every vendor must accept the Infosys Supplier Code of Conduct as part of onboarding.

Documents: for Indian suppliers, expect to provide PAN, GST registration and bank details (usually a cancelled cheque or bank letter). Overseas suppliers are asked for tax forms, for example W-9 or W-8BEN-E for US-related cases.

Supplier diversity: the policy covers suppliers of people, services and goods and aims to give diverse suppliers a fair chance to compete.

New vendor set-up and changes: the AP Vendor Master team handles new vendor set-up and changes to existing vendor data, such as bank account, address or GST details, at APVendor_master@infosys.com. Existing vendors can also review, request changes to and certify their details on the vendor certification portal. Send change requests from your official company email, with supporting documents.

Beware of fraud: Infosys will not ask you to change bank details over a phone call or a personal email. If you receive such a request, verify it through your known Infosys procurement contact before acting.

title: Visiting the Electronics City campus: visitor passes and security
body:
Infosys does not publish its campus visitor rules online, so this article describes the generic visitor process used at large Indian corporate campuses. Your host's instructions and the security desk on the day take priority.

Address: the registered office and main Bengaluru campus is at Electronics City, Hosur Road, Bengaluru 560 100. The published main phone number is +91 80 2852 0261. Electronics City has several Infosys buildings, so confirm the exact building with your host.

Before you arrive:
1. Your Infosys host raises a visitor request in advance. You receive a pass number, date, and the gate you should use.
2. Carry a valid government photo ID (Aadhaar, passport, driving licence, voter ID or PAN card). The name must match the pass.
3. Arrive 15–20 minutes early to allow for security checks.

At the gate: security verifies your ID and pass, may photograph you, and issues a visitor badge that must be visible at all times. Your host normally escorts you inside.

Common rules at corporate campuses: laptops and storage devices may need to be declared; photography is usually restricted; and visitors stay in approved areas.

On this help desk, signed-in visitors can ask "status of my visitor pass <number>" to see the demo pass with date, host and gate. If the pass is missing or the details are wrong, contact your host first; they must reissue it.

title: Unclaimed dividends and shares moved to IEPF
body:
This summarises Infosys's shareholder-services pages on unclaimed dividends.

The rule: under Section 124 of the Companies Act, 2013, a dividend that remains unpaid or unclaimed for seven years must be transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF). Shares on which dividends have not been claimed for seven consecutive years are also moved to an IEPF demat account.

Before the transfer: claim through Infosys's registrar and transfer agent, KFin Technologies Limited. Infosys publishes the list of shareholders whose dividends are due for transfer, along with deadlines. As of October 2026, its page asks holders to claim the FY2019-20 interim dividend through KFin by 5 November 2026, and says requests received from 3 August 2026 to 5 November 2026 are processed only through electronic credit to the bank account. The page also shows an earlier date, so confirm your deadline with KFin.

After the transfer: shares and dividends already moved to IEPF can still be claimed by applying online to the IEPF Authority in Form IEPF-5, following the IEPF procedure.

Contacts (as of October 2026):
- KFin Technologies: einward.ris@kfintech.com, toll free 1800 309 4001, Selenium Tower B, Plot 31 & 32, Financial District, Nanakramguda, Hyderabad 500 032.
- Infosys investor relations: investors@infosys.com.

Keep your bank details and KYC updated so future dividends are credited directly and do not become unclaimed.

title: Tax on Infosys dividends: TDS, Form 15G and 15H
body:
Dividends are taxable in the hands of shareholders, and Infosys deducts tax at source (TDS) as required. This summarises the FY2025-26 dividend communication and the 2025-26 buy-back tax FAQ published by Infosys; check the notice for the current dividend before acting.

When TDS applies: for resident individuals, TDS is deducted only if total dividends paid by Infosys in the financial year exceed a threshold. The FY2025-26 interim dividend notice set it at Rs 10,000 (it was Rs 5,000 in the FY2024-25 notice).

No-TDS declarations: if you have a valid PAN updated with your depository (NSDL/CDSL) or with KFin, you can submit:
- Form 15G, if you are a resident individual under 60 and your estimated total income stays below the basic exemption limit (the FAQ lists Rs 2,50,000 under the old regime and Rs 4,00,000 under the new regime).
- Form 15H, if you are 60 or older.
Forms are uploaded on the Infosys shareholder portal before the cut-off date given in each dividend notice.

No valid PAN: a 15G/15H without a valid PAN is not accepted, and tax is deducted at a higher rate (20% per the FAQ).

Already deducted? Infosys cannot refund tax it has deposited. You claim credit for it when you file your income tax return.

Questions on dividend tax: dividend.tax@infosys.com.

title: Updating KYC, bank and nomination for your shares
body:
Dividends can only be paid directly to your bank account if your KYC is up to date. Infosys's investor-service pages explain who to approach.

Shares in demat form: update PAN, address, bank account, email, mobile and nomination with your depository participant (your broker or bank DP). Infosys and KFin take these details from the depository records.

Shares in physical form: send requests to the registrar, KFin Technologies, using the SEBI forms published on Infosys's investor-services page:
- Form ISR-1: register or change PAN, KYC details, bank account, address, email or mobile.
- Form ISR-2: confirm or update your signature (bank attestation).
- Form ISR-3: opt out of nomination.
Send them to einward.ris@kfintech.com or to KFin's Hyderabad address.

Frozen folios: SEBI required physical holders to furnish PAN, KYC and nomination. Folios without these details were frozen by the registrar, and dividends on such folios are paid only after the details are updated (Infosys's 2024 AGM notice says this applies from 1 April 2024).

Physical transfers: as of October 2026, Infosys notes a special window from 5 February 2026 to 4 February 2027 for re-lodging physical transfer deeds; such shares are credited only in demat form with a one-year lock-in.

Consider converting physical shares to demat; transfers of physical shares are otherwise not permitted.

title: Recruitment fraud: how to spot a fake Infosys job offer
body:
Infosys has published a recruitment fraud alert because scammers post fake openings, run fake interviews and send fake offer letters to collect money or personal data.

What Infosys says about its genuine process:
- Infosys never asks for fees of any kind, during or after hiring. Any request for a registration, training, laptop, security deposit or visa fee is a scam.
- Hiring always includes at least one interview, virtual or in person. Infosys does not interview over instant messaging apps.
- The recruitment team does not ask for bank account details, tax forms or credit card information during hiring.
- Recruiters write from @infosys.com addresses. Mails from Gmail, Yahoo or similar addresses are a red flag, and scammers can also spoof the @infosys.com display name, so stay alert.

Check an offer: for Infosys Limited in India, offer letters are available on the official careers site after you log in, and the site has an offer validation page (career.infosys.com/offerValidation). Do not trust a PDF that only arrived by email or WhatsApp.

If you were targeted: stop all contact, do not pay or share documents, and report it to the police or the cybercrime portal immediately. Keep screenshots of messages and payment details as evidence.

This help desk cannot confirm offers. If in doubt, use the official validation page or the careers site.

title: Offer letters, joining and background verification
body:
This article combines what Infosys publishes on its careers and privacy pages with a generic description of corporate onboarding.

Offer letters: for Infosys Limited in India, offers are made available on the official careers site after you log in, where you can also validate and accept them. Infosys's careers material states that offers are no longer shared by email, so treat emailed offer PDFs with caution.

Background verification (BGV): Infosys's privacy statements say background checks are run only after a candidate is selected or shortlisted, through an authorised third-party agency where applicable. Details collected can include passport details and information needed for the background check. Some client engagements may require additional checks, such as criminal or health-related checks.

What BGV generally covers at Indian employers (generic): identity, education certificates, previous employment (relieving letters, experience letters, payslips), address and, where permitted, criminal records. Typical problems are mismatched dates of joining or leaving, unverifiable institutions and name mismatches across documents.

Before joining (generic): keep originals of your degree certificates, mark sheets, relieving letters, PAN and Aadhaar ready; check that your name and date of birth match across documents; and share your existing UAN so PF continues in the same account.

Remember: genuine onboarding never asks you to pay a fee. See the recruitment fraud article if anything feels off.

title: Raising a concern: whistleblower and grievance channels
body:
Infosys publishes a Whistleblower Policy and describes its reporting channels in its governance and ESG pages. As of October 2026, these channels are listed:

Who can report: directors, employees and any other person, including vendors, contractors, consultants, trainees, shareholders, former employees and job applicants.

How to report:
- Employees can speak first to their manager, HR manager or the helpline.
- Email: whistleblower@infosys.com, or the Chief Compliance Officer at complianceoffice@infosys.com.
- Ethics helpline web portal: infosys.speakuptrust.com, which is run by an independent third party.
- If you are not comfortable approaching the compliance office, you can write to the chair of the Audit Committee at Audit.Committee@infosys.com.
- Suppliers can report breaches of the Supplier Code of Conduct to whistleblower@infosys.com or vendorincident@infosys.com.

Anonymity and protection: you may report anonymously, and the policy prohibits retaliation against anyone who raises a concern in good faith.

Other dedicated channels for employees, as published: workplace behaviour concerns to HEAR@infosys.com, and sexual harassment complaints to the grievance redressal body at GRB@infosys.com.

What to include: what happened, when and where, who was involved, and any documents. Concrete facts help the investigation.

This help desk is not a confidential channel. Do not post whistleblower details in a support ticket; use the channels above.

title: Infosys Foundation and CSR: focus areas and grant requests
body:
Infosys carries out much of its corporate social responsibility (CSR) work through the Infosys Foundation. This summarises the Foundation's about page, the FY2026-27 CSR annual action plan and the CSR policy.

Focus areas: the Foundation's primary themes are education, healthcare, women empowerment and environmental sustainability. Secondary themes include art and culture, rural development, destitute care and disaster relief. The FY2026-27 action plan lists education and skills, healthcare including preventive health, environmental sustainability, gender equality and women's empowerment, and other areas such as arts and heritage, disaster relief and animal welfare.

Requesting a grant (for NGOs): the Foundation accepts grant requests through a dedicated online portal linked from its website. Under the CSR policy, requests can be submitted throughout the year. A panel of experts evaluates proposals that fall within the focus areas and prioritises them by expected impact. The Board's CSR Committee gives final approval.

Tips for applicants: make sure your organisation is legally registered and eligible to receive CSR funds under Indian law, align the proposal clearly with one focus area, and include measurable outcomes and a budget.

Individuals seeking personal financial help should note that the Foundation works through projects and partner organisations. Requests for donations made in Infosys's name by phone or social media should be checked against the official website.

title: Who to contact at Infosys for what
body:

Shareholders:

Employees (generic process): payslip, leave, PF and Form 16 questions go to HR or payroll through your internal HR portal. On this help desk you can check your own demo payslip and leave balance, or raise a ticket.

Visitors: contact your Infosys host to arrange or change a visitor pass.
